headline: Chattogram: Mother and daughter killed in home attack
summary: A 40-year-old woman and her 16-year-old daughter were hacked to death in Anwara Upazila; a five-year-old child was also injured.
details: A mother and her 16-year-old daughter were hacked to death in their own home in Chattogram’s Anwara Upazila on Saturday night.
The victims have been identified as Annie Barua, 40, and her daughter Priyanti Barua, 16, residents of Purba Konnara village in Paroiakora Upazila.
According to Mahmudul Hasan, assistant superintendent of Chattogram District Police (Anwara Circle), unknown perpetrators entered the home at night and attacked the two with sharp weapons.
The attack also left a five-year-old child injured, though police stated the injuries are not critical.
Police officials noted that Annie’s husband, Sujon Barua, works as a guard in Chattogram city and was not at home during the incident.
Preliminary investigations suggest the killings may have been linked to disputes with close relatives, according to the ASP.
Police are currently following up on leads and working to arrest the perpetrators.
caption:

According to Mahmudul Hasan, assistant superintendent of Chattogram District Police (Anwara Circle), unknown perpetrators entered the home at night and attacked the two with sharp weapons.

The attack also left a five-year-old child injured, though police stated the injuries are not critical.

Police officials noted that Annie’s husband, Sujon Barua, works as a guard in Chattogram city and was not at home during the incident.

Preliminary investigations suggest the killings may have been linked to disputes with close relatives, according to the ASP.

Police are currently following up on leads and working to arrest the perpetrators.

headline_marked: VAR chaos: [[FIFA admits technical outage]] during Qatar-Switzerland match
headline: VAR chaos: FIFA admits technical outage during Qatar-Switzerland match
summary: A technical glitch prevented offside animations from appearing during a pivotal penalty decision, sparking debate over the tournament's technology reliability.
details: Qatar and Switzerland played to a 1–1 draw in their Group B opener at the 2026 World Cup. However, the match was overshadowed by a fierce controversy surrounding a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) decision.

The conflict began in the 13th minute when Switzerland was awarded a penalty after a collision between Qatar goalkeeper Mahmud Abunada and Remo Freuler. Breel Embolo converted the penalty to give Switzerland a 1–0 lead.

Confusion erupted as replays suggested two potential offside positions in the buildup to the penalty. However, the broadcast did not show the usual VAR offside animation graphics, leaving players and viewers in the dark.

Hours after the match, FIFA issued an official statement acknowledging a 'brief technical outage' that prevented the onside animation graphic from being generated for the 14th-minute penalty decision.
FIFA insisted that the outage did not affect the VAR process itself, stating that officials had access to all necessary tools and that the lines used did not show the attacking player to be offside.

Despite the clarification, analysts and fans expressed frustration. Former player Gary Neville noted that the lack of real-time visual confirmation raised questions about transparency in the tournament's technology.
The incident has sparked early concerns about the reliability and consistency of VAR operations at the 2026 World Cup, turning a hard-fought draw into a debate over technology.
caption:

The conflict began in the 13th minute when Switzerland was awarded a penalty after a collision between Qatar goalkeeper Mahmud Abunada and Remo Freuler. Breel Embolo converted the penalty to give Switzerland a 1–0 lead.

Confusion erupted as replays suggested two potential offside positions in the buildup to the penalty. However, the broadcast did not show the usual VAR offside animation graphics, leaving players and viewers in the dark.

Hours after the match, FIFA issued an official statement acknowledging a 'brief technical outage' that prevented the onside animation graphic from being generated for the 14th-minute penalty decision.

FIFA insisted that the outage did not affect the VAR process itself, stating that officials had access to all necessary tools and that the lines used did not show the attacking player to be offside.

Despite the clarification, analysts and fans expressed frustration. Former player Gary Neville noted that the lack of real-time visual confirmation raised questions about transparency in the tournament's technology.

The incident has sparked early concerns about the reliability and consistency of VAR operations at the 2026 World Cup, turning a hard-fought draw into a debate over technology.
